title: Integrate with the Referrer Policy spec, part 2 of n
body:
This makes getting the referrer policy a first-class citizen of the
environment settings object algorithm set. WorkerGlobalScopes and
Documents both get referrer policies, and the process by which the
header or meta element set these is spelled out explicitly. This
includes tricky cases like navigation and `<iframe>`s, which the Referrer
Policy spec currently handles with (somewhat incomplete and incorrect)
monkeypatches.

Closes the following Referrer Policy issues:
- https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-referrer-policy/issues/30
- https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-referrer-policy/issues/32

and is part of the larger effort at https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-referrer-policy/issues/43

/cc @bzbarsky @jeisinger @estark37 @mikewest 

I think there are two important questions outstanding before this is mergeable:
- Is the "copying" of referrerpolicy for various nested browsing contexts correct? https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-referrer-policy/issues/30, https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-referrer-policy/issues/31, and https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-referrer-policy/issues/32 all touch on that. I assumed here the desire was to snapshot the creator document's referrer policy at new-document creation time. This leads to the potential issue pointed out by @bzbarsky in https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-referrer-policy/issues/31. An alternative is to have the new document's referrer policy point upward to the creator document, unless overridden by a meta tag; this seems messier though.
- I did not understand the intent of https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-delivery-implicit-workers. There is no such thing as "the Worker's incumbent settings object". If I were to interpret it as "the incumbent settings object at the time the Worker constructor is running," then on the face of it, what that algorithm says is that doing `new Worker()` will override your document's referrer policy and reset it to `"no-referrer-when-downgrade"` (i.e., this is a third way to set your document-wide policy, in addition to the HTTP header and the meta element). That seems clearly wrong. What was the intent of that section?

Also, @bzbarsky @annevk, I was a bit unsure how to reify the "local scheme nested browsing contexts inherit". I think I did it, but that section could use careful review. I don't think the navigate algorithm is very explicit about local schemes at the moment; it might be my patch is the best we can do until more navigation cleanup happens.

This should allow the following sections of Referrer Policy to become more informative and get trimmed down:
- https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#integration-with-html
- https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-delivery-implicit
- https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#terms (definition of referrer policy no longer needs to patch environment settings object)
- https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#set-referrer-policy (can be removed)
